title: AI Use Disclosure Decision Helper
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: Practice activity in which learners apply a five-rule illustrative lab disclosure policy (not a real venue's policy) to eight scenarios of AI use in an electrical engineering project, choosing one of four actions for each: Disclose in the paper, Record in the project log only, No disclosure needed, or Not permitted. Each scenario has one attempt in a fixed order with feedback naming the matching rule and the reason. The run ends with a score out of 8, a mastery statement at 7 of 8, and an illustrative draft disclosure statement assembled from the scenarios that required disclosure in the paper.

educational.topic: Disclosure and citation of AI use in research publications
learningObjectives: Apply a five-rule illustrative lab disclosure policy to eight scenarios of AI use and give the required action for each, with at least 7 of 8 correct
Distinguish disclosure in the paper from a project log entry and from no record
prerequisites: AI disclosure, citation of AI use, and authorship policy from the section Integrity, Disclosure, and Authorship of Chapter 18

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; the action list and buttons are native HTML controls reachable with the Tab key; correct and incorrect feedback uses words and check-mark or X symbols as well as color, and the matching rule is marked with an arrow as well as an outline; the color pair is the color-blind-safe Okabe-Ito blue and vermillion; the base text size is chosen per width from 18 px down to 14 px (13 px only below about 340 px wide) so that every state fits.

controls.label: Choose an action...
controls.purpose: Chooses one of the four actions: Disclose in the paper, Record in the project log only, No disclosure needed, Not permitted. Disabled after the answer is submitted.

controls.label: Submit
controls.purpose: Commits the chosen action for the current scenario (one attempt per scenario). Enabled once an action is chosen.

controls.label: Next Scenario / See Score
controls.purpose: Enabled after the answer is submitted. Advances to the next scenario, and after scenario 8 shows the score, the mastery statement, and the draft disclosure statement.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Rule application to fixed-order cases with one attempt each, immediate feedback naming the matching rule, and a synthesis step that assembles a draft disclosure statement
keyQuestions: What does the policy require here?
Does the AI-assisted text, code, data, or figure appear in the submitted paper or contribute to reported results?
Is the use only grammar, spelling, or formatting assistance?
Would the action list an AI system as an author?
commonMisconceptions: If AI was used heavily, it can be listed as an author
Any use at all must be disclosed in the paper
assessmentOpportunities: At least 7 of 8 scenarios answered with the action the policy gives on the first attempt is evidence of mastery
Reading the policy is exploration and is not evidence of mastery
